newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian Telekom sees rise in 1996 net profit.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian Telekom sees rise in 1996 net profit.

text.p: Slovenian Telekom said on Monday it expected its 1996 net profit to rise to three billion tolars ($21.1 million) on higher revenue, a 200 million tolar increase from the previous year.
"For Slovenian circumstances this may look like a big profit, but it is not sufficient for a proper development of the Telekom's network," Adolf Zupan, general manager of Telekom, told Reuters.
Zupan said revenue in 1996 rose to 42 billion tolars from 38 billion tolars in 1995 and predicted revenue would reach 48 billion next year.
Telekom's investments in 1996 rose to 18 billion tolars from 13 billion in the previous year.

"Most of our investments are intended for development and modernisation of the telecommunications network, which we expect to become comparable to the average standard of European Union countries by the end of the century," Zupan said.
Telekom expects to reach its target of 42 telephone lines per 100 inhabitants by the year 2000, up from current 33.3 and nearer to the EU average of some 50 lines per 100 inhabitants.

Zupan said this goal would be hard to achieve with current prices of domestic phone calls, which are about six times lower than the EU average, while international call prices are similar to those in the EU.

"Too low prices of domestic telephone calls are also a cause for a slow development of the network, therefore we expect to raise them to 50 percent of the EU average by 1999," Zupan added. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
